scope: Fresh-process focused save/migration acceptance smoke over the repository own isolated in-memory IndexedDB backend, the real SaveRepository, the real CampaignDirector and the real CombatEngine. No repository method is overridden, stubbed or mocked.
notCovered: A real browser IndexedDB: the backend is the repository own deterministic in-memory IDBFactory, not Chromium.
The renderer, the UI layer and physical input devices: no browser was opened and no interaction was driven.
A full test suite: this is one focused smoke, not a suite run.

observedFindings.observation: The live access rule in src/game/campaign/access.ts applies the permanent exile only inside its "id === 'solkar'" branch. A Canopy/Fang/Shadow leader whose faction leaderStatus is "exiled" (representative present:false) still reads as available; those three leaders are bound by the "absent" status instead. Vara (Sky) and Sable (Pack) are envoys and are bound by neither.
observedFindings.why: Reported as observed, not asserted as desired. The authored story only exiles Solkar, so no production path writes an exiled status for another faction. This smoke observed the rule by writing that status directly into a checkpoint; it is a statement about the current rule, not a defect claim and not a proposed change.
observedFindings.where: checks named "[<id>] a non-Crown leader is bound by absence, not by exile" and "[<id>] the envoy is not removed by its faction's leader status".

observedFindings.observation: The schema-1 migration recruited only the companions whose legacy Heartroot fragment the save held: Vara (Sky) and Koro (Canopy). Asha, Sable, Nyra and Solkar stayed unrecruited, and the schema-1 role-slot party { scout: vara, utility: koro } was reduced to the single travelling companion id koro, which the migration had earned.
observedFindings.why: Confirms the conservative derivation: the migration never grants a companion the legacy save did not evidence.
observedFindings.where: checks named "the legacy Sky fragment recruited Vara" through "the legacy save did not recruit Solkar" and "the legacy role-slot party reduced to the Combat-primary Koro, which the migrated roster earned".

observedFindings.observation: Reading the seeded schema-1 slot migrated the envelope in memory only: the stored row bytes were unchanged and the raw recovery export still returned schemaVersion 1.
observedFindings.why: Confirms the read-boundary migration contract on the real repository over the isolated backend.
observedFindings.where: checks named "the stored legacy rows were not rewritten by the read" and "the raw recovery export still returns the original schema-1 envelope".

fixtures.legacy: A schema-1 envelope built from the repository own documented legacy shape (a schema-1 world without a companion roster, a role-slot party, a Koro Dominion ledger entry and no session metadata), seeded into the slots/runs stores of the production database.
fixtures.roster: The migration derives the roster with the production schema-1 rules (fragments plus covenant tier); no rule was re-implemented in this file.
fixtures.combat: A real serialized CombatEngine state per companion id, with a travelling instance, a narrative instance of the same species, a stale mark, a stale support slow, a stale job and a stale object request.
fixtures.region: The real authored Greenwake region plus the real ChapterParty projection, loaded through the real CombatEngine.loadRegion.

cleanupApi.listSlots: SaveRepository.listSlots(): Promise<SaveSlotSummary[]> — every slot of this repository scope, newest updatedAt first.
cleanupApi.removeSlot: SaveRepository.removeSlot(slotId: string): Promise<void> — deletes exactly one slot row from the scope database; no other row is touched.
cleanupApi.storeScope: The scope selects the whole IndexedDB database name. The "slots" and "runs" object stores live inside that one database; a production repository never reads or writes the candidate database and vice versa.
cleanupApi.slotRowShape: The stored slot row is the summary fields plus "envelope": [format, schemaVersion, scope, kind, runId, checkpoint, campaign, progress, eventKeys, savedAt].
cleanupApi.autosaveSlotId: autosave:<runId> — one stable autosave slot per run; a manual slot is slot-<id>.
cleanupApi.runLedger: The "runs" store holds one ledger row per runId (runId, kind, dominionHistory, eventKeys, updatedAt). removeSlot does not delete a ledger row.
cleanupApi.safeCleanupRule: List first, select by explicit runId, remove only those slotIds, and never delete an unknown row wholesale.
